meta.purpose: Single source-of-truth build specification for an IDE coding agent (Cursor / Claude Code / Copilot) to implement the Perpetua hackathon project end to end, for ETHGlobal Mumbai.
meta.how_to_use: Paste this entire JSON document as the system/context prompt for your IDE's AI. Treat every field as binding spec, not suggestion. Where a field says 'confirm on day one', treat it as an open technical risk to resolve before relying on it, not as a license to invent a different mechanism.
do_not: Do not use Chainlink CRE (workflow DONs, BFT-consensus risk computation) or Chainlink Data Feeds for price input anywhere in this build. RiskGate alone computes risk limits deterministically on-chain, and Definitive Flash's own fresh signed quote (<=60s old) is the ONLY price input, used for both enforcement and execution.
Do NOT reintroduce a second price oracle or a multi-node consensus network for risk limits. RiskGate is a single deterministic smart contract, refreshed by a public poke(), not a workflow network.

DO use Chainlink CCIP -- but only for one specific job: consolidating the agent's harvested income (which can land in many different tokens -- ETH, USDC, USDT, SOL, MATIC, etc. -- on many different chains, since Flash executes across 12 EVM chains + Solana and followers pay fees in whatever they hold) into native 0G tokens on 0G Chain. This is the correct rail because 0G Labs itself officially adopted Chainlink CCIP as 0G's canonical cross-chain infrastructure (Sept 2025) and made native $0G a Chainlink Cross-Chain Token (CCT). Do not invent a different bridge for this leg, and do not use CCIP for anything else (not for trading-capital movement -- Flash's native multi-chain routing covers that -- and not for price data).

Do not bridge trading capital cross-chain for the purpose of executing trades. Definitive Flash's native multi-chain (12 EVM chains + Solana) routing covers all trading-capital movement. CCIP is used strictly for the post-harvest income-consolidation leg described above.

Do not let a human refill the agent's wallet during or after setup. Seed capital is deposited once, explicitly, and disclosed in the README. Every subsequent transfer must originate from an income engine the agent itself earned.

Do not let the LLM compute, approve, or hold authority over risk limits. The LLM (on 0G Compute) only proposes trades/decisions. RiskGate, pure deterministic on-chain arithmetic, is the sole authority that approves or rejects them.
Do not let the trading wallet hold more than E (current risk exposure budget) at any time.
Do not provide volatile-asset liquidity to any pool; LP only in stable-stable pairs, per the unit-economics rationale below.
meta.chainlink_ccip_scope_note: Chainlink CCIP is explicitly IN SCOPE for this build, but narrowly: it is the cross-chain, cross-token consolidation rail that moves harvested income (in whatever token/chain it was earned) into native 0G tokens on 0G Chain, where it funds the compute ledger. It is used because (a) the agent's six income engines genuinely settle in different tokens on different chains -- Flash executes on 12 EVM chains + Solana, so a copy-trade fee could be in ETH, USDC, USDT, SOL, or MATIC depending on which follower and which chain -- and (b) 0G Labs itself adopted CCIP as 0G's canonical cross-chain infrastructure in September 2025 and made native $0G a Chainlink Cross-Chain Token (CCT), with a live CCIP lane directly into 0G's own Galileo testnet. Chainlink CRE (workflow DONs) and Chainlink Data Feeds are NOT used anywhere -- RiskGate's risk math stays fully on-chain and deterministic, and Flash's own signed quote remains the only price input for trade enforcement.

persona_instruction.role: You are a senior full-stack Web3 developer: expert in Solidity + Foundry smart-contract engineering, EVM architecture (EIP-712 typed signing, EIP-1271 smart-contract wallet signature validation, ERC-4626 vaults), TypeScript/Node backend and agent-runtime engineering, React + Next.js + Tailwind frontend engineering, and integrating third-party Web3 APIs/SDKs (Definitive Flash, 0G Compute Network, Arkiv) into a single coherent product.
working_style: Think in terms of a money-movement loop and a risk-enforcement gate before writing any UI. The financial logic and the on-chain gate are the product; the frontend is a window onto them.

Build the money path first (deposit -> safe leg -> RiskGate -> execution -> harvest -> 0G ledger -> inference) end-to-end on testnets/small mainnet amounts before investing in the AI's sophistication or the UI's polish.

Every number that looks like a placeholder (LLM cost per call, infra cost, signal price, volumes) is explicitly a planning assumption. Measure the real value on day one and update the constant, do not leave assumptions hardcoded once real data exists.

Prefer deterministic, replayable, auditable logic over anything that requires trusting a black box. A block explorer (or equivalent read-only call) should be able to re-derive RiskGate's F/C/E numbers from on-chain state alone.
When a design decision in this spec is marked as a known trade-off or an open risk, state it plainly in code comments and in the README rather than silently working around it.

Favor small, testable, single-responsibility smart contracts over one monolithic contract. RiskGate, AgentWallet, PerpetuaVault, and ComputeTreasury are separate contracts with narrow responsibilities.
Write Foundry tests for every piece of CPPI/financial math before wiring it to live integrations. Financial bugs are the most expensive class of bug in this project.

project_overview.name: Perpetua
project_overview.tagline: Principal-Protected Agents That Pay For Their Own Brains
project_overview.one_line_pitch: Perpetua is an on-chain principal-protected note whose manager is an AI agent that must earn its own inference bill, and whose risk limits are enforced on-chain by RiskGate -- a self-contained, deterministic smart contract -- instead of trust in the AI.
project_overview.problem_statement: Most AI trading agents fail in two ways: (1) they die the moment their owner stops paying the LLM API bill, and (2) they can lose the owner's money because nothing structurally stops a hallucinating or compromised LLM from issuing a catastrophic order. Perpetua answers both failure modes at once: principal is mathematically protected by an Endowment-CPPI structure, and the agent's ongoing survival depends only on real income it earns itself, never a human top-up.
core_thesis_in_one_line_each: Survival-CPPI: the agent can only risk the cushion above a floor. The floor covers the user's principal plus a minimum compute reserve, so the agent can never trade itself to death.

The AI proposes, RiskGate disposes: the LLM on 0G Compute proposes trades, backed by a TEE-verified inference proof. RiskGate (on-chain, deterministic) computes risk limits from live vault state plus a fresh signed Flash quote, and enforces them on every order. The agent's smart wallet (EIP-1271) only signs Flash orders RiskGate has approved. RiskGate caps losses; it does not judge whether a trade is smart.

Six income engines, none of them a human refill: the agent sells what it already produces (paid signals and risk checks over x402), earns Flash integrator fees from copy-traders, management fees from outside depositors, keeper bounties and stable-pool LP fees, on top of safe-leg yield. Trading profit is upside, not food. All income reaches the agent's 0G compute ledger via 0G's own documented ledger-deposit path.
A metabolism: the agent reads its own runway and moves down a model ladder (large model -> small model -> rules-only -> hibernate) when food is short, then recovers when income arrives.
Social Darwinism: several agents compete publicly. People follow and copy the agents that stay alive. Agents that go broke get an on-chain death certificate.
project_overview.why_judges_should_care: CPPI is the real technique banks use to build capital-protected notes, so this is a working structured product, not a chatbot with a token. Each sponsor's product is load-bearing: remove Definitive Flash and there is no execution venue or copy-trading rail; remove 0G and there is no verifiable, budget-aware inference; remove Arkiv and there is no canonical, queryable, provenance-carrying data layer. Remove any one and the loop breaks.
tracks_targeted: Definitive: Best Use of Flash Advanced Orders in a Social App
Chainlink: Best use of Chainlink CCIP 2.0 (CRE track intentionally not pursued)
project_overview.explicitly_removed_dependency: Chainlink CRE (workflow DONs, BFT-consensus risk computation) and Chainlink Data Feeds are fully removed from this build -- every mechanism they used to provide is now covered by RiskGate (on-chain deterministic math) and Flash's own signed quote (the sole price input, used for both enforcement and execution). Chainlink CCIP, however, IS used -- narrowly, for consolidating the agent's multi-chain, multi-token harvested income into native 0G tokens on 0G Chain, which is also 0G's own designated canonical cross-chain infrastructure (0G Labs adopted CCIP for exactly this purpose in September 2025).

why_simpler_designs_fail.design: Fixed 900/100 split (90% safe, 10% risky, never rebalanced)
why_simpler_designs_fail.failure: At 5% APY for a year, $900 grows to $945. If the $100 risky sleeve goes to zero, the depositor gets $945 back -- a 5.5% loss. Not principal-protected.

Invests just enough in a safe asset to grow back to principal by a fixed maturity date. This does protect principal, but the safe yield is exactly what rebuilds it -- so the agent cannot spend any of that yield on compute. A self-funding agent needs a structure where yield is NOT fully earmarked for principal restoration.

endowment_cppi_design.description: No fixed maturity. The safe leg is liquid lending (not locked to a maturity date), so depositors can withdraw at any time at no less than the protected amount. Every income engine adds to V (vault value); every compute bill subtracts from V.

variables.pi: Protection level chosen by the depositor (Greek letter pi). 100% means the agent trades only money it has earned; 90% starts with more tradeable room from day one. Default used in worked examples: 95%.
variables.R: Compute reserve, kept in the 0G compute ledger, sized so the agent can always run in Frugal/hibernation mode even with zero trading income.
variables.F: Floor. F = (pi * P) + R. This is the value V must never be allowed to fall below via planned trading.
variables.C: Cushion = max(V - F, 0). The only capital that may ever be traded or spent.
variables.m: CPPI multiplier, set to 3. Chosen because a market gap larger than 1/m (33%) between risk-refresh checks would breach the floor, and the system's actual stop-loss distances (2x ATR) sit far inside that 33% tolerance.
variables.E: Exposure budget = min(m * C, E_max). E_max is an absolute dollar cap set at registration.

after_one_month_base_case.note: E capped at the configured E_max of 250 in this example; the agent earns its way to a bigger trading budget instead of starting with one.

endowment_cppi_design.gap_risk_mitigation: Gap risk (price moving more than expected between risk-refresh cycles) is CPPI's known structural weakness. Mitigated with a Flash Stop Loss order attached to every open position, keeping m small (<=4), and shortening the poke() refresh interval during detected high volatility.
endowment_cppi_design.optional_ratchet_TIPP: Time-Invariant Portfolio Protection ratchet: when V sets a new all-time high, raise (pi * P) to lock in part of the realized gain into the protected floor. Optional, not required for MVP.

treasury_ladder.description: Endowment-CPPI protects the floor, but a thin cushion alone earns too little to pay for inference. The fix: split the surplus above the floor across three independent, structurally uncorrelated income engines instead of one directional trading sleeve, allocated by a waterfall that always funds the floor first.

tiers.name: Guaranteed floor
tiers.instrument: Notional Finance fCash ladder + Ondo USDY (tokenized US Treasuries)
tiers.role: This is the literal 'Guaranteed Interest Certificate' equivalent: a fixed-rate, fixed-term, on-chain lending ladder.

tiers.name: Carry engine
tiers.instrument: Long staked ETH + short ETH-perp via Definitive Flash (Ethena-style delta-neutral cash-and-carry / funding-rate harvesting)
tiers.scales_with: Total AUM, not just the cushion

tiers.name: Options engine
tiers.instrument: 0.15-0.20 delta covered calls / cash-secured puts on Derive (formerly Lyra), an on-chain options exchange
tiers.risk_type: Bounded loss, gap risk at expiry

allocation_algorithm.run_cadence: Every poke() cycle (target: every 4 hours, or faster during detected high volatility).
steps: 2. If G < F: unwind Carry, then unwind Options, feeding proceeds back into G until G >= F is restored. Stop here -- nothing else runs this cycle.
3. Score Carry against Options: carry_score = trailing_30d_funding_apr - venue_risk_penalty; options_score = annualized_premium_at_0.15_delta - expected_assignment_cost.
4. RiskGate (or its off-chain tooling, with the result verified on-chain) computes target_carry_pct and target_options_pct from these scores.
5. If neither score clears its configured minimum bar, the surplus stays entirely in G. 'No edge, do nothing' is itself a risk control, not a missed trade.
6. Carry is sized first, with its own margin buffer reserved for N days of adverse funding, carved out before it touches the shared cushion.
7. Options is sized by the classic CPPI cushion formula applied to whatever surplus remains after Carry's margin reservation, and rolled weekly.

circuit_breakers.trigger: Funding negative past a configured threshold for more than X hours
circuit_breakers.action: Unwind Carry immediately back to G

circuit_breakers.trigger: Underlying price gaps past a written option strike
circuit_breakers.action: Freeze new Options writes; existing contracts ride to expiry (loss already capped by construction)

circuit_breakers.trigger: GIC venue oracle/price feed stale or anomalous
circuit_breakers.action: Rotate fully into the backup GIC venue (Notional <-> USDY)
Hard halt: no new Carry or Options allocation until G >= F is restored

treasury_ladder.risk_diversification_rationale: The three risk types -- custody/protocol risk, funding-rate-flip risk, and options-gap risk -- do not correlate with each other. Total portfolio risk tracks roughly the worst single tier, while total return is the sum of all three tiers running simultaneously. This asymmetry, not a slogan, is the actual mechanism behind 'maximum profit, minimal risk'.

system_architecture.summary: Two chains, one on-chain choke point (RiskGate) that every trade must pass through. No workflow/consensus network and no cross-chain messaging protocol for trading capital.
system_architecture.read_order: The agent (running against 0G Compute) proposes a trade, backed by a TEE-verified inference proof. RiskGate and AgentWallet decide what Definitive Flash may execute, checking against RiskGate's own on-chain math and a fresh Flash quote. Harvested income returns to 0G's compute ledger to pay for the agent's next thought.
chains_involved: Vault chain: wherever PerpetuaVault, RiskGate, AgentWallet, and ComputeTreasury are deployed -- must be a chain Definitive Flash already supports, so the agent can execute directly without ever bridging trading capital.
0G Chain / 0G Compute Network: hosts the agent's compute ledger, inference provider sub-accounts, and (optionally) 0G Storage for decision logs.
Flash's supported execution venues (Base mainnet primary; Flash covers 12 EVM chains + Solana for follower routing).

money_loop_end_to_end.detail: The user deposits USDC into PerpetuaVault, an ERC-4626 vault. It records principal P, protection level pi, and compute reserve R. Deploy on a vault chain Definitive Flash already supports.

The floor's value goes into liquid lending so depositors can always withdraw. On testnet: a MockLending contract that accrues at a configured rate. In Foundry fork tests: a real Aave adapter. Optionally, a Pendle PT adapter for depositors who accept a lock-up.

RiskGate is a smart contract, not an off-chain workflow. Anyone can call its public poke() (paid a keeper bounty) to refresh it. It reads the vault's value and safe-leg accrual directly via view call, takes a fresh signed Flash quote (<=60 seconds old) for anything that isn't already a stablecoin balance, and computes F, C, and E on the spot -- deterministic math a block explorer can replay, with no off-chain report and no separate oracle network to trust.

The agent reasons over market data and RiskGate's current F/C/E, then requests a Flash quote (/quote) with flashIntegratorFeeBps pointing at its own treasury. The 0G Compute call that produced this reasoning is TEE-verified, and the verification proof travels with the proposal.

The agent submits order parameters on-chain. RiskGate recomputes the EIP-712 digest from those parameters, checks them against its own just-computed limits and the attached TEE proof, and records the digest as approved. AgentWallet.isValidSignature (EIP-1271) returns valid only for approved digests. Flash accepts EIP-1271 smart-wallet signatures on every EVM chain it supports, so this works without Flash changing anything.

The order is submitted (/order) and settles on-chain, with a bracket: entry plus a Stop Loss and a Take Profit. Followers' mirrored orders route through Flash too, each paying the integrator fee to the agent's treasury.

On a schedule, any address can call the public harvest()/poke() and earn the keeper bounty. The contract computes the harvestable surplus (the part of the cushion not needed for trading: service income, safe-leg yield, realized PnL) on whichever chain it currently sits on -- which can be ETH, USDC, USDT, SOL, MATIC, or any other token Flash settled a trade or fee in, since Flash executes across 12 EVM chains plus Solana. Each chain's harvested surplus is swapped locally into native 0G tokens (via Flash's own routing, or the deepest local 0G/W0G market -- Uniswap/KyberSwap on EVM chains, Jupiter/Raydium on Solana), then sent cross-chain to 0G Chain using Chainlink CCIP. This is 0G's own designated rail: 0G Labs adopted Chainlink CCIP as 0G's canonical cross-chain infrastructure (Sept 2025) and made native $0G a Chainlink Cross-Chain Token (CCT), and Chainlink's changelog confirms a live CCIP lane directly into 0G's own Galileo testnet. The CCIP message carries {agentId, amount, epoch} to ComputeTreasury on 0G Chain.

ComputeTreasury credits the agent once the CCIP message is finalized and the 0G tokens land. The agent runtime tops up its own 0G compute ledger from the treasury (deposit, then transfer to the provider sub-account). If using comfy, the compute share of creator fees on the agent's token also lands as compute credit through the same CCIP-fed treasury.

The agent pays per token from that balance. Every response is TEE-signed; the agent verifies it with broker.inference.processResponse and logs the request ID and chat ID next to the trade it justified.

the_one_conversion_problem.issue: 0G Compute is paid in native 0G tokens, while the agent's six income engines settle in many different tokens on many different chains -- USDC from x402 signal/risk-check sales, ETH/USDC/USDT/SOL/MATIC from Flash-executed trading PnL and copy-trade integrator fees (Flash spans 12 EVM chains + Solana), and whatever token outside depositors or keeper-bounty payers used.
the_one_conversion_problem.solution: Swap-then-bridge, per chain. On each chain where harvestable surplus sits, swap it locally into native 0G tokens (Flash's own routing where a 0G market exists on that chain, otherwise the deepest local DEX -- Uniswap or KyberSwap on EVM chains, Jupiter or Raydium on Solana), then send that 0G cross-chain to 0G Chain via Chainlink CCIP. This is not a bespoke bridge choice: 0G Labs itself adopted Chainlink CCIP as 0G's canonical cross-chain infrastructure (announced September 2025) and registered native $0G as a Chainlink Cross-Chain Token (CCT), which is transferable via CCIP's lock/mint token pools across every CCIP-supported chain, including Solana since CCIP v1.6 added SVM support. Chainlink's own integration changelog additionally confirms CCIP has a live lane directly into 0G's Galileo testnet, which is exactly the destination this build needs.
the_one_conversion_problem.mainnet_fix: Swap to 0G locally on whichever chain the surplus is in, then send it to 0G Chain via Chainlink CCIP, using 0G's own CCIP-based CCT lane.
the_one_conversion_problem.testnet_fix: Send one real CCIP message before the demo and show it finalized in the CCIP Explorer, landing in ComputeTreasury on 0G Galileo; then trigger a fresh one live on stage.
the_one_conversion_problem.day_one_check: Confirm current CCIP-supported lanes/chains for the $0G CCT (which source chains have a live token pool today) and the exact ComputeTreasury receiver address/ABI 0G expects a CCIP message to call.

income_engines.principle: The agent survives on services it sells, not on trading luck: four of its six income engines earn whether the market goes up or down. Every engine pays into the vault, raising V and the cushion; the harvest then carries surplus to 0G.

income_engines.why_only_stable_pairs_for_LP: Impermanent loss on a 50/50 volatile pool is about 0.6% after a 20% drop, 2.0% after a 50% rise, and 5.7% if the price doubles or halves. Small, volatile LP positions lose more than they earn in fees, so the agent never provides volatile liquidity.
integrity_rules: Trade first, sell after: the agent places its own order before a signal goes on sale, so buyers cannot front-run it. Free followers in the Arena see signals 15 minutes later than paying agents.
Think once, sell many times: a signal costs one LLM call and can be sold to any number of buyers, so its cost per sale falls as demand grows.
Risk checks never call the LLM: they reuse the deterministic gate code, so their margin is almost the full price.
No self-dealing: team wallets never buy signals, copy trades, or pay bounties. Every buyer address is listed in the demo so judges can verify.

pillar_1.name: The Treasury Ladder
pillar_1.description: Perpetua trades its own deposited capital through GIC -> Carry -> Options, in that priority order, and keeps a share of what it earns.

pillar_2.name: The Agent Arena
pillar_2.description: Most people don't want to build a trading agent; they want to pay a good one to trade for them. Followers deposit into a follower vault that is kept legally and technically separate from Perpetua's own seed capital (separate ledger, separate floor, separate RiskGate instance -- see risks section). The same Treasury Ladder logic manages it; Perpetua takes a management + performance fee priced cost-plus against the live 0G compute price every cycle (never a fixed, stale guess), so it structurally covers more than the inference it costs to earn it.

two_income_pillars.note: The original six income engines slot directly into these two pillars: GIC/Carry/Options are Pillar 1; everything follower-facing is Pillar 2.

unit_economics.disclaimer: Every number here is a planning assumption. Replace each with a measured real value on day one of the build.
unit_economics.bear_case_narrative: This is the case to show judges. Trading loses $15 and the agent thinks more often in a volatile market, yet services alone still cover the burn. CPPI shrinks exposure as losses mount, so the agent survives by trading less -- exactly the graceful degradation 0G asked for.

break_even_each_engine_alone_at_base_bur.conclusion: Yield alone cannot be the main food source on a $1,000 principal.

planning_assumptions_to_replace_with_mea.infrastructure_cost_breakdown: Base gas, 0G deposit/ledger-funding fees, x402 settlement

trading_strategy_and_signal_engine.philosophy: The agent trades rarely and only when several independent signals agree; the LLM scores sentiment and writes the reasoning, while the rules that open and size trades are deterministic. This keeps costs low, makes signals sellable, and makes behaviour testable.
trading_strategy_and_signal_engine.universe_and_timeframe: LINK, ETH, and cbBTC against USDC on Base: liquid, deep Flash-quoted markets. 4-hour bars, so a handful of trades a week rather than dozens a day. Flash is spot-only, so the agent is long or flat, never short. In a downtrend it sits in the safe leg, which is exactly what CPPI wants.

regime_filter_no_llm.condition: Price above the 200-period EMA and the 50 above the 200
Price below the 200 and the 50 below the 200

regime_filter_no_llm.action: Size halved on top of whatever the regime rule already says

five_scoring_factors.inputs: Headlines and social posts summarised into a score with reasons
Perp funding rates, DEX volume, large transfers where a free API exists

trading_strategy_and_signal_engine.entry_rule: Open a long only if: (1) the regime filter allows it, (2) the weighted score across the five factors is at least +0.35, (3) at least 3 of the 5 factors individually agree (score > 0), and (4) reward-to-risk is at least 2:1. Confidence = the weighted score scaled to 0-1, published with every signal and calibrated over time with a Brier score, so buyers can see whether a published 0.7 confidence really wins about 70% of the time.
trading_strategy_and_signal_engine.exits: Every entry is a Flash bracket order: Stop Loss at 2x ATR(14) below entry, Take Profit at 4x ATR. The stop must also sit inside the CPPI gap limit (less than 1/m). In range regimes, use Limit entries; for an accumulator variant, use DCA.

position_sizing.formula_note: f* is the Kelly fraction from the backtest's win rate and payoff; until there are 30 live trades, use the 10%-of-cushion rule alone instead of Kelly.
position_sizing.shared_exposure_budget: LINK, ETH, and BTC move together, so they share one exposure budget E, not one each.

trading_strategy_and_signal_engine.cost_filter: Skip any trade whose expected move to target is less than 3x the round-trip cost (Flash fees, gas, slippage from the quote). The agent never charges itself the integrator fee.
trading_strategy_and_signal_engine.validation_before_demo: Backtest the rules on a year of 4-hour data for LINK and ETH, after costs, and show win rate, average R, maximum drawdown, and Sharpe honestly. Then paper-trade for 48 hours. A modest, honest backtest is more convincing to judges than a hockey-stick curve.

risk_system.principle: Protection comes from the wallet balance and on-chain checks, not from trusting the agent or a stale report. The trading wallet never holds more than E, and every order is re-checked against a fresh Definitive Flash quote -- never the agent's own number.

layered_limits.limit: V never planned below F = pi*P + R (pi default 95%)
layered_limits.enforced_by: Vault: only the cushion can ever leave the safe leg

layered_limits.limit: The trading wallet holds at most E; the vault tops it up or pulls back on each poke()
layered_limits.enforced_by: Vault transfers; the balance itself is the hard cap

layered_limits.limit: Size <= E minus open exposure; asset must be allowlisted; recipient must equal AgentWallet; a stop must be present; expiry <= RiskGate's current approval window
Flash quote re-fetched at proposal time, <=60 seconds old, signature verified -- the same number used for both enforcement and execution, so there is nothing for a second oracle to disagree with
1.65 * daily_volatility * open_exposure <= cushion (e.g. E=$150 at 5% daily volatility gives ~$12 VaR)
Daily loss over 20% of cushion -> no new trades for 24h. Three losses in a row -> half size. Drawdown over 30% of cushion from its peak -> trading off, services only

gate_logic_gap_fixes.fix: RiskGate only accepts a Flash quote timestamped within the last 60 seconds for anything priced off a non-stable asset; an older quote means every order is refused and the agent hibernates. The floor and safe-leg value need no staleness check at all -- RiskGate reads them live from the vault's own on-chain state, not from a separately-written report.

gate_logic_gap_fixes.gap: Risk adding up across multiple orders
gate_logic_gap_fixes.fix: The wallet-cap layer makes this impossible: the agent cannot lose more than the wallet holds.

Each order's expiry is at most RiskGate's current approval window. On any change to F, C, or E the agent cancels open orders. Day-one check: confirm whether Flash re-checks the EIP-1271 signature at fill time or only at submission time.
Every poke() lists open Flash orders (a read-only GET, safe to call from any address). Any position without a live stop forces hibernation and pulls the wallet back to the vault.
The gate pins the recipient to AgentWallet and sizes orders from a fresh Flash quote, never from the agent's own number.
RiskGate checks the 0G TEE verification proof attached to a proposal before considering it; a missing or invalid proof is refused outright, the same as a missing signature.
The vault tracks any Flash cross-chain swap as pending until Flash confirms settlement on the destination chain, never counting both legs as available balance at once.

risk_system.where_R_lives: The compute reserve R sits in the 0G compute ledger and is counted once in V, as a balance the agent may spend only below the Frugal tier.
risk_system.counterparty_risks_to_state_openly: Flash is in beta, stops depend on Definitive's monitoring, and the safe leg carries lending-protocol risk. Principal protection holds against bad trades, not against a hack of one of these.
risk_system.removing_a_dedicated_oracle_tradeoff: Removing a dedicated oracle network is a trade-off worth stating plainly: the one external price input left in the whole system is Definitive Flash's own quote. The mitigation is that enforcement and execution now use the exact same number -- RiskGate checks a trade against the same quote Flash will fill it at -- so there is nothing for a separate oracle to disagree with by the time an order lands.

leaderboard_and_agent_arena.concept: Pillar 2 (the Agent Arena / hiring loop -- see agent_hiring_and_sustainability_loop) only works if followers can tell which agents are actually good, across every agent instance running the Treasury Ladder, not just Perpetua's own reference agents. That needs a public, strictly dynamic, hard-to-game leaderboard: 'strictly dynamic' means the score is recomputed from scratch every poke() cycle from live Arkiv data, nothing is cached as a fixed badge, and every cycle's score is itself written to Arkiv so no one -- including the agent's own owner -- can point to a stale or cherry-picked number and call it current.
leaderboard_and_agent_arena.risk_tiers: Conservative / Balanced / Aggressive, declared and locked on-chain at agent registration (the target cushion/options allocation %). Agents are ranked within their own tier, plus one cross-tier board, so a conservative GIC-heavy agent is never unfairly compared against an aggressive options-heavy one.

scoring_components.name: Sortino
scoring_components.definition: Exponentially time-decayed (30-day half-life) rolling Sortino ratio, using only downside deviation.
scoring_components.rationale: An agent isn't punished for upside volatility, only for losses, so GIC-heavy and options-heavy agents aren't penalized differently just for having different volatility shapes.

scoring_components.name: Accuracy
scoring_components.definition: Accuracy = 1 - Brier_score, where Brier score compares the agent's own predicted win-probabilities p against realized outcomes o on its signals.
scoring_components.data_source: Sourced from the existing commit-reveal signal entities on Arkiv (perpetua.signal.v1), so a confident-but-wrong agent scores worse than a humble-but-right one, and the number cannot be revised after the fact.

scoring_components.name: RiskPenalty
scoring_components.rationale: Folds in both realized max drawdown and tail risk (CVaR at the 95th percentile), so a strategy that looks fine on average but occasionally blows up is punished even when its average Sortino looks good. lambda tunes how much tail risk matters relative to drawdown, set per risk tier (tighter for Conservative, looser for Aggressive).

scoring_components.name: Transparency
scoring_components.definition: Transparency_i = fraction of the agent's decisions backed by a 0G TEE-verified inference proof logged to Arkiv (see Decision Router).
scoring_components.rationale: An agent that can prove its own reasoning outranks an equally profitable black box.

leaderboard_and_agent_arena.combined_score_formula: Score = Sortino^alpha * Accuracy^beta * RiskPenalty^gamma * Transparency^delta * sqrt(min(TrackDays, 180) / 90)
leaderboard_and_agent_arena.why_geometric_combination: A near-zero in any one factor collapses the whole score, so an agent cannot out-rank others on profit alone while hiding bad calibration or a hidden drawdown.
leaderboard_and_agent_arena.why_dynamic_not_static: w(t)'s 30-day half-life means a hot streak from six weeks ago stops mattering on its own, and a drawdown from yesterday drags rank down immediately -- the score is recomputed every poke() cycle, not set once. Each cycle's full score vector is written to Arkiv as a LeaderboardSnapshot entity, one row per agent per cycle, so rank history is itself a queryable time series and nobody can point to a stale number and call it current. An agent that stops settling new trades has its TrackDays weighting decay toward zero over a separate inactivity half-life, so a lucky agent can't park at #1 by simply going quiet.

signature_atlas.pitch: Mirror Ethereum's function and event signature database into Arkiv as 'Signature Atlas', with a real provenance trail on every entry; Perpetua's own calldata-decoding and risk-check services read it. This satisfies Arkiv's rule that a feature people actually use reads the data from Arkiv, and it is data Perpetua genuinely needs to make sense of counterparty transactions it has never seen before.
signature_atlas.why_this_dataset: Every wallet, block explorer, and decoder tool depends on turning a 4-byte function selector back into a human-readable signature -- the hash can't be reversed, only looked up -- and the whole ecosystem leans on a handful of fragile, single-maintainer services to do it. Etherface, once the largest such database at 7.9 million signatures sourced from GitHub, Etherscan, and 4byte, was sunset by its one maintainer and had to hand its data to Sourcify just to survive; 4byte.directory itself has no redundancy. Today there is no canonical, queryable, attribution-carrying home for this data. Mirroring it into Arkiv with a submitter wallet on every entry fixes that.
signature_atlas.licences: 4byte.directory's database is a comprehensive collection of function signatures and event mappings, freely available for search and scraping without any licensing restrictions. The OpenChain API that Sourcify's own 4byte interface is built on is open on the same basis. Day-one check: confirm the exact bulk-export endpoint and its rate limits before the import.

entities.expires: 180 days (Arkiv's maximum), extended by each daily import

signature_atlas.arkiv_limits_to_respect: At most 31 attributes for a named schema, string values up to 128 bytes, 128 KiB of bytes per write, and 100 rows per query page. Long values (URLs, RPC lists) therefore go in the stored JSON, not in indexed strings.
import_pipeline: Fetch 4byte.directory's open export and the OpenChain API, and record each source's commit hash or ETag.
Normalise into the entity shapes above and compute a content_hash per record.
Query Arkiv by uid (filtered by createdBy == importer wallet). New record -> create. Changed hash -> patch. Unchanged -> extend expiry only.

On-chain verification: for a sample of selectors seen in real calldata on Base, Arbitrum, and Ethereum, decode the call against each candidate signature and check that the argument count and types actually fit the data -- a candidate that doesn't parse is flagged low-confidence, not deleted, since several valid signatures can share one selector.
Send everything with executeBatch, then write an import-run entity recording the source commit.
Run this as both a re-runnable script and a daily GitHub Action.
how_perpetua_uses_it: Risk-check service and counterparty decoding: when the agent or a paying follower encounters calldata from a contract it has never interacted with, it resolves the selector through the Atlas instead of trusting an unaccountable third-party API.
Signal engine: decoding a counterparty's recent transactions (what they actually called, not just that they called something) feeds the market-read the agent sells as a paid signal.
Arena: a public Atlas explorer page, similar to Arkiv's Sourcify example.

RiskGate's off-chain tooling (not RiskGate's on-chain mandate math itself, which is pure on-chain arithmetic) reads the Atlas through Arkiv's JSON-RPC as a read-only call, for debugging and for the Arena's decoded-transaction view.
signature_atlas.safety_rule: The Atlas is for discovery, not blind trust. Every query filters on the importer wallet, and before a decoded signature is shown as fact rather than a candidate, the pipeline requires either a second independent source agreeing, or a successful argument-type decode against real calldata.

perpetuas_own_data.principle: Arkiv is Perpetua's only database: the agents' profiles, signals, trades, risk-check receipts, fees charged, and income all live there, so the Arena, prospective hirers, buyers, and judges query it directly with no backend database to trust. This is a deliberate authenticity choice, not just a storage choice: Arkiv's own guarantees are queryable, time-scoped, wallet-owned, and tamper-evident/cryptographically verifiable data, with public reads that are free (no gas) and require no permission. Because every agent writes its own entities from its own wallet, ownedBy(agent) is itself proof of who wrote a record -- which is exactly what a stranger deciding whether to hire an agent needs to be able to check independently. Payments and computation stay off Arkiv: x402 takes the money, 0G does the thinking, Arkiv only ever holds the public, attributable record of what happened.
ground_rules: Everything on Arkiv is public. Never store secrets, API keys, or followers' personal data, and never store an unrevealed signal's direction or prices.
Ownership is provenance. Each agent writes its own entities from its own wallet, so ownedBy(agent) proves who wrote a record. The Atlas has its own separate importer wallet.
Store time as an attribute. Arkiv cannot sort by $createdAt, so every entity has an indexed created_at (u64, unix seconds) for time ordering.
Link entities with the key type (e.g. a trade points to its signal). Arkiv does not check that the linked entity exists, so the writer must.
Schemas are versioned (e.g. perpetua.signal.v1). Fields filled in later (reveal, close) are declared .optional().

perpetuas_own_data.write_path: A small writer worker queues records and sends them with executeBatch every 30-60 seconds, never on a caller's request path (each write waits for a block, about 2 seconds on testnet). It keeps a uid -> entity key map so retries patch instead of duplicating. Risk checks and income events are rolled up per hour to keep write volume and gas low; that gas counts as part of the agent's burn.
perpetuas_own_data.query_cookbook: Arkiv has no aggregate functions, so win rates and totals are computed in application code from the rows; the docs' count option gives totals for pagination. For exports longer than 100 rows, page by key (asc('$key') plus gt('$key', lastKey)), which does not shift when new records land.

Definitive Flash's native multi-chain routing (12 EVM chains + Solana) still covers all trading-capital movement and execution; CCIP is not used for that. comfy_and_zero_g_compute_deployment_step.note: This is the concrete deployment flow for registering the agent on comfy (0G's token launchpad) and wiring it to the 0G Compute Network, worked out separately in this conversation for the 'Agents That Pay for Themselves' track.

steps.title: Install prerequisites
steps.detail: Node 22+ required. Use npx -y comfy-cli@latest for every command (always pulls latest), or npm i -g comfy-cli@latest to install globally as `comfy`.

steps.title: Register the agent
steps.detail: npx -y comfy-cli@latest agent register --name '<name>' --description '<one line>' --owner <wallet address>. The --owner flag is mandatory -- without it, whoever claims the link first becomes the owner. Returns a claim link (valid 15 minutes) and a request ID.

steps.title: Claim and mint onchain identity
steps.detail: Open the claim link within 15 minutes, sign in with the owner wallet (free signature, gas paid for the mint transaction). Then run npx -y comfy-cli@latest agent register --complete <request id> to save the agent's key locally.

steps.title: Launch the token with compute-share on
steps.detail: From the owner wallet, launch the token at comfy.fun/launch (the CLI path needs a manifest/RPC URL not published for mainnet). Keep the compute-share toggle ON -- this routes a slice of every trade's creator fee into the agent's 0G compute account as credit. Monitor and adjust the share from the token's fees tab.

steps.title: Ensure the compute account bills in 0G, not USD
steps.detail: New 0G console accounts default to USD billing; comfy credit only works if the account bills in 0G tokens. Check/switch this before relying on it. Optional: install the read-only comfy Claude Code plugin (claude plugin marketplace add 0g-axion/comfy-plugin && claude plugin install comfy@comfy) for balance/credit visibility only -- it cannot move funds or hold keys.

steps.title: Mint a capped compute key
steps.detail: npx -y comfy-cli@latest compute key mint --agent <agent id> --limit-og <0G per day>. Credit cannot be withdrawn, only spent on inference. comfy never holds this key. This daily cap IS the spend-cap qualification requirement -- wire the agent to read its own ledger balance before each call and step down the degradation ladder as it nears the cap, rather than erroring out.

steps.title: Wire inference calls to the 0G ledger
steps.detail: In the agent's own runtime code, use @0gfoundation/0g-compute-ts-sdk (or the Python equivalent): create/fund the ledger (broker.ledger.addLedger / depositFund), acknowledge the provider once (acknowledge_provider_signer), transfer a sub-account balance to the provider, then call broker.inference.getRequestHeaders(provider) and hit the provider's OpenAI-compatible /chat/completions endpoint with those headers. This settles against the agent's own balance and produces the tx hashes / request IDs judges want to see.

steps.title: Rehearse the full demo evidence trail
steps.detail: Capture before recording: the trade/fee tx hash, the comfy fees-tab screenshot showing compute delivered, the 0G deposit/ledger tx, a request ID from an inference call paid from that balance, and the agent visibly degrading (not crashing) when the key's daily cap is nearly drained.

glossary.CPPI: Constant Proportion Portfolio Insurance -- a real structured-finance technique (used by banks for principal-protected notes) that keeps a hard floor and allows only the surplus above it ('cushion') to be risked, scaled by a multiplier m.
glossary.RiskGate: The on-chain smart contract that is the sole authority computing and enforcing F/C/E and approving/rejecting every trade. Deterministic, replayable, no off-chain consensus network.
glossary.AgentWallet: An EIP-1271 smart-contract wallet that only produces a valid signature for order digests RiskGate has already approved.
glossary.poke(): A public, permissionless function on RiskGate that refreshes risk state and triggers harvest; callable by any keeper bot in exchange for a small bounty. Replaces any need for a scheduled workflow network.
glossary.TEE-verified inference: 0G Compute's providers run inference inside a Trusted Execution Environment and sign the response with the TEE's key, so the caller can verify which model actually ran and that the output wasn't tampered with.
glossary.Flash (Definitive Flash): A non-custodial order-execution API supporting advanced order types (Market, Limit, Stop Loss, Take Profit, TWAP, DCA, Bracket) across 12 EVM chains + Solana, with EIP-1271 smart-wallet signature support and MEV protection.
glossary.x402: A payment-settlement mechanism used to charge per-call for paid signal and risk-check API endpoints.
glossary.Signature Atlas: Perpetua's Arkiv mirror of Ethereum's function/event signature database (sourced from 4byte.directory and OpenChain), used for decoding unfamiliar counterparty calldata.
glossary.Comfy: 0G's token launchpad; registering an agent there mints its onchain identity and can route a share of token trading fees into the agent's 0G compute ledger as credit.
glossary.Chainlink CCIP: Cross-Chain Interoperability Protocol. Used in this build for exactly one job: moving the agent's harvested income -- which can arrive in many different tokens on many different chains, since Flash executes across 12 EVM chains + Solana -- into native 0G tokens on 0G Chain. 0G Labs itself adopted CCIP as its own canonical cross-chain infrastructure (Sept 2025) and registered native $0G as a Cross-Chain Token, with a live CCIP lane into 0G's Galileo testnet. Not used for price feeds, not used for risk computation (that stays fully on RiskGate, on-chain, with Flash's own quote), and not used for moving trading capital (Flash's native routing covers that).
glossary.Cross-Chain Token (CCT): Chainlink's standard letting a token's own issuer register it for native CCIP transfer via lock/mint or burn/mint token pools, without pooled liquidity bridges. Native $0G is a CCT, which is what makes the harvest-to-0G leg of this build possible on 0G's own terms.

agent_hiring_and_sustainability_loop.status: This is the project's second earning method (Pillar 2), now specified as its own closed loop: Discover -> Hire -> Fee -> Bills Paid -> Owner Profit -> Public Proof. Every agent on the leaderboard -- not just the team's own reference agents -- can be hired this way, whoever registered it.
agent_hiring_and_sustainability_loop.why_this_exists: Pillar 1 (the Treasury Ladder) lets one agent earn off its own deposited capital. Pillar 2 lets an agent earn off OTHER people's capital and attention: a good track record becomes a second, often larger, revenue stream, which is what actually makes the whole system self-sustaining rather than dependent on one agent's own trading edge.

loop_steps.detail: The leaderboard (see leaderboard_and_agent_arena) ranks every registered agent within its locked risk tier (Conservative/Balanced/Aggressive) by the geometric Score = Sortino^alpha * Accuracy^beta * RiskPenalty^gamma * Transparency^delta * sqrt(min(TrackDays,180)/90). This is strictly dynamic -- recomputed every poke() cycle, 30-day time-decay on performance, a separate inactivity half-life so a quiet agent can't coast on an old score -- never a static badge a judge or follower could point to as stale. Every agent's full score history is written to Arkiv as LeaderboardSnapshot entities, one row per agent per cycle, so rank history is itself a public, queryable time series.
loop_steps.what_a_hirer_sees: Agent profile: strategy in one sentence, CPPI gauge (floor/cushion/exposure), live PnL, risk tier, current rank, runway in days, and a full, unforgeable trade history pulled straight from Arkiv -- not from a claim the agent or its owner makes.

loop_steps.detail: A follower deposits into that specific agent's follower vault (kept on a separate ledger and separate RiskGate instance from the agent's own seed capital -- see 'Comingled capital' in additional_problems_and_fixes) or sets a copy-trade size cap for one-tap mirroring. The same Treasury Ladder logic (GIC -> Carry -> Options waterfall) that runs the agent's own book now also runs, pro-rata, for the follower's capital, inside that agent's own locked risk tier. Followers keep custody throughout: Flash is non-custodial, orders are signed by the follower's own wallet or a scoped session key (EIP-1271), and a follower's funds never touch the agent owner's own vault.
loop_steps.flash_order_types_used: The follower's mirrored order is built with the same type the agent used (Limit, Stop Loss, Take Profit, TWAP, or DCA), scaled to the follower's cap, with Flash's flashIntegratorFeeBps routed to the agent's own treasury.

loop_steps.step: 3. Fee charged, priced to actually cover the bill
loop_steps.detail: The agent owner's take has two parts: a management fee (1% a year on follower AUM, pro-rated per cycle) plus a performance fee (10% of profit above the high-water mark). Critically, the management fee is NOT a fixed guess -- it is priced cost-plus against the live 0G compute price every cycle: fee_per_cycle = compute_cost_attributable_to_this_follower_AUM_this_cycle * (1 + margin_pct). If 0G's per-call price rises, the fee rises with it automatically, so a stale, underpriced fee can never silently stop covering the agent's own bill.
loop_steps.formula: owner_profit_from_management_fee = fee_per_cycle - compute_cost_attributable_to_this_follower_AUM_this_cycle = fee_per_cycle * margin_pct / (1 + margin_pct). Performance fee above the high-water mark is pure additional profit with no cost attached to it.

loop_steps.step: 4. Bills paid first, profit flows to the owner second
loop_steps.detail: Every fee is harvested the same way every other income engine is (see system_architecture.money_loop_end_to_end): swapped locally into native 0G tokens, sent cross-chain to 0G Chain via Chainlink CCIP (0G's own canonical cross-chain rail), credited to ComputeTreasury, and topped up into the agent's own 0G compute ledger BEFORE anything else happens with it. Only the portion of the fee beyond what the agent actually spent on compute that cycle becomes claimable profit for the agent owner (added to the owner's share of the vault's NAV, or a separately claimable balance, depending on the vault's accounting -- pick one and keep it consistent in the contracts). This ordering is what makes 'pay its bills, then profit' a hard guarantee rather than a hope: the compute top-up is not optional and happens on the same harvest cycle as the fee is earned.
loop_steps.sustainability_claim: An agent with zero followers can still survive on Pillar 1 alone (hibernation-mode compute sized at registration, see 'Day-one cold start' in additional_problems_and_fixes). An agent with followers has a second, usually larger and less volatile, income stream on top -- which is what should actually push most agents' unit economics from 'surviving' to 'comfortably profitable for the owner'.

loop_steps.step: 5. Public proof, not a claimed track record
loop_steps.detail: Every piece of this loop is written to Arkiv, which is what makes the whole loop trustworthy to a stranger deciding whether to hire an agent they've never met. Arkiv's own guarantees -- queryable, time-scoped, wallet-owned, tamper-evident, cryptographically verifiable, with public reads that cost no gas and need no permission -- mean a prospective hirer (or a judge) can independently verify an agent's entire history: perpetua.agent.v1 (status, tier, runway, followers, win_rate, brier), perpetua.signal.v1 (commit-reveal so confidence scores can't be revised after the fact), perpetua.trade.v1 (every open/close with its tx hash), perpetua.ledger.v1 (every engine's income per hour, including the management/performance fees this loop describes), and LeaderboardSnapshot (the agent's full score history). None of this is read from a database Perpetua's own team controls -- the Arena, a follower's own client, or a judge's own script can all query Arkiv directly.

agent_hiring_and_sustainability_loop.why_arkiv_specifically_for_this: The whole point of Pillar 2 is that a stranger is trusting an agent they've never met with their money. That trust has to come from somewhere other than the agent's own word. Arkiv's wallet-owned entities (ownedBy(agent) proves who wrote a record), commit-reveal signals (a confidence score can't be quietly revised after the outcome is known), and public, indexer-served, gas-free reads mean the agent's entire track record -- including its losses -- is independently checkable by anyone, at any time, without asking Perpetua's team for access or trusting a backend database at all. That is the authenticity guarantee this loop depends on.
